text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

The panel's composition proves nothing on its own. Women are a majority in education, so an all-female panel in a school hiring process is statistically unremarkable, and panels of one sex don't systematically favour their own. Leading with it makes you look aggrieved rather than wronged, and it hands them an easy way to dismiss everything else you say.

Your real grievance is substantive and much stronger: on paper you hold a master's in educational leadership and five years of actual leadership experience against her short courses. Push hard on the unanswered request — written reasons are normally an entitlement, and the delay is itself telling. Ask for the scoring criteria and how each candidate was rated.

If those reasons never arrive, or are evasive, that's when a pattern becomes worth arguing.
